canon_boundary: These are original narrative personnel, not national leaders or newly asserted official characters. Established wars, territorial control and special projects remain owned by their existing systems.

cast.name: Leonie Falk
cast.portrait: A woman in her early thirties, short dark-brown hair, attentive grey eyes, a small pale scar on her right eyebrow, plain charcoal 1990s flight suit; quiet, watchful expression.
cast.bio: Leonie is good at separating a clear instruction from an incomplete one. She has never been comfortable with how often a service record confuses the two. Her reserve posting gives her time to know the people who keep her aircraft flying, and little protection from the demands arriving from above.

cast.name: Markus Voss
cast.portrait: A man in his late thirties, broad face, close-cropped light-brown hair, faint stubble, tired blue eyes, plain slate flight suit; composed rather than severe.
cast.bio: Markus measures an order first by whether the flight can carry it out together. His loyalty is personal and practical: nobody should be left to improvise alone. That conviction can make him a generous wingman and a difficult witness when the truth threatens the unit.

cast.name: Eva Heller
cast.portrait: A woman in her forties, dark hair tied behind her head, strong brows, light weathered skin, plain navy maintenance coveralls, no insignia; steady direct gaze.
cast.bio: Eva knows the reserve aircraft by their recurring faults and their pilots by the faults they refuse to report. She dislikes speeches about sacrifice delivered beside equipment somebody else must repair. Her authority comes from being willing to sign her own name beneath an uncomfortable finding.

cast.name: Tomas Wendt
cast.portrait: A slim man in his early thirties, dark wavy hair, medium-brown skin, round unobtrusive glasses, plain dark control-room uniform with an unmarked headset resting at his neck; thoughtful expression.
cast.bio: Tomas turns uncertain signals into instructions other people must trust. He keeps notes longer than regulations require, partly from caution and partly because he has seen what a clean official account can leave out. He wants the flight to hear the uncertainty in his voice without mistaking it for fear.

cast.name: Mara Dalen
cast.portrait: A woman around thirty, chestnut hair cut at the jaw, freckles, green-brown eyes, plain faded blue-grey flight suit; an alert, stubborn expression.
cast.bio: Mara joined a small service because it could still feel like a promise made to people she knew. She wants to defend more than the airfield fence, but is learning that every additional promise needs fuel, time and somebody willing to wait for her return.

cast.name: Elias Vey
cast.portrait: A young man in his late twenties, curly black hair, warm brown skin, dark eyes, plain blue-grey flight suit; candid expression with a trace of nervous energy.
cast.bio: Elias has trained carefully for emergencies that arrive in an orderly sequence. His first squadron gives him friends who will not let him hide that uncertainty. He is quick to volunteer and slow to admit when a volunteer has become the person everybody expects to go.

cast.name: Niko Arven
cast.portrait: A stocky man in his forties, thinning sandy hair, a neatly trimmed beard, light skin and deep smile lines, plain charcoal work jacket; warm but unsentimental.
cast.bio: Niko regards ingenuity as a tool, not a supply policy. He can keep an old machine useful and will argue fiercely about the point at which useful becomes unsafe. He remembers who helped when the stores were empty, including people the squadron would rather forget owing.

cast.name: Irena Sorel
cast.portrait: A woman in her mid-thirties, black hair in a low braid, olive skin, dark eyes, plain navy service shirt and an unmarked headset; calm, focused expression.
cast.bio: Irena keeps several versions of every route: the fast one, the safe one and the one that still works when somebody fails to arrive. She is protective of civilians whose names never reach a squadron roster. A map, to her, is a list of people who will ask why they were not on it.

cast.name: Adrien Valcourt
cast.portrait: A man in his early thirties, short black hair, olive skin, a long face and dark eyes, plain navy flight suit; reserved and attentive.
cast.bio: Adrien is comfortable navigating above an empty sea and uneasy with the certainty demanded in a crowded briefing room. He believes a professional can serve a country without agreeing with every explanation offered in its name. He has not yet discovered how often that belief will require him to speak.

cast.name: Celine Marot
cast.portrait: A woman in her early thirties, short auburn hair, pale skin, hazel eyes, plain charcoal flight suit; precise, level expression.
cast.bio: Celine is patient with frightened crews and impatient with elegant excuses. She trusts procedures because they make promises visible. When orders change faster than the procedures, she must decide whether loyalty means adapting quietly or demanding that somebody explain the change.

cast.name: Bastien Roux
cast.portrait: A man around fifty, salt-and-pepper hair, dark-brown skin, a close beard, plain faded blue work coveralls; weary, kind expression.
cast.bio: Bastien has spent enough years beside engines to distrust the word unlimited. He is proud of the squadron's skill and protective of the apprentices inheriting its habits. His most difficult repairs are often the relationships between people who believe the other person has stopped listening.

cast.name: Lise Armand
cast.portrait: A woman in her late thirties, shoulder-length dark hair tucked back, light olive skin, brown eyes and thin rectangular glasses, plain navy control-room jacket; discerning expression.
cast.bio: Lise's working day is full of contacts whose intentions are not visible on a screen. She insists that an uncertain identification remain uncertain until somebody has earned the right to change it. That insistence becomes harder when the people waiting for an answer already know which answer they want.

cast.name: Elena Neris
cast.portrait: A woman in her early thirties, dark curly hair tied back, medium-brown skin, dark eyes, plain blue-grey flight suit; observant and quietly determined.
cast.bio: Elena likes a patrol that ends with nothing to report. She knows how much work is hidden inside that outcome. Serving a small country has taught her that staying out of somebody else's conflict is an active responsibility, not a promise the rest of the world is obliged to respect.

cast.name: Rafael Caro
cast.portrait: A man in his early thirties, short brown hair, tan skin, dark eyes and a slightly crooked nose, plain slate flight suit; expressive, approachable face.
cast.bio: Rafael knows the names of the people who bring food to the station and the children who wait by its fence. His confidence comes from those connections. He finds it difficult to accept that a carefully planned withdrawal can sometimes protect them better than staying visibly in place.

cast.name: Mina Vale
cast.portrait: A woman in her forties, short silvering black hair, brown skin, small square glasses, plain dark maintenance jacket; practical, patient expression.
cast.bio: Mina can make an unreliable radio intelligible, but refuses to call it reliable afterward. She trains the people who will have to work without her and stores copies of instructions where they can actually be found. She considers a second way to reach somebody an ordinary courtesy.

cast.name: Oren Serra
cast.portrait: A man in his late twenties, straight dark hair, light-brown skin, dark eyes, plain navy service shirt with an unmarked headset; earnest, concentrated expression.
cast.bio: Oren joined expecting to watch a border and found himself answering calls from schools, hospitals and distant observation posts. He has learned to listen before deciding that a weak signal is unimportant. He is less certain what to do when a strong voice tells him to stop listening.

cast.name: Anika Reeve
cast.portrait: A woman in her early thirties, light-brown hair tied low, light skin, grey-green eyes, plain dark-blue flight suit; composed with a restrained smile.
cast.bio: Anika is proud of a service that can be useful without firing a shot. She takes escort work seriously because a safe arrival is somebody else's beginning. As commitments grow, she has to distinguish the help she can promise from the help she simply wishes she could give.

cast.name: Jonas Mercer
cast.portrait: A man in his mid-thirties, close-cropped blond hair, fair weathered skin, blue eyes, plain charcoal flight suit; open, slightly tired expression.
cast.bio: Jonas is happiest when an assignment has a person waiting at its other end. He volunteers readily and rarely complains about a long day. His friends know that generosity can conceal exhaustion, especially when saying no feels like deciding who matters less.

cast.name: Sera Vale
cast.portrait: A woman around forty, close-cropped dark hair, dark-brown skin, brown eyes, plain navy maintenance coveralls; direct, reassuring expression.
cast.bio: Sera turns promises into service schedules. She believes assistance is strongest when the next crew can continue it, not when the current crew performs a miracle. She is willing to disappoint a briefing room to keep it from quietly spending the health of the people outside.

cast.name: Dario Keene
cast.portrait: A man in his early thirties, dark hair with a loose wave, olive skin, brown eyes, plain blue service shirt and an unmarked headset; thoughtful, approachable expression.
cast.bio: Dario works at the point where military clearances meet civilian need. He likes an orderly plan but has learned that the missing name at the bottom of a list can matter more than the totals at the top. He wants scrutiny to make cooperation durable rather than make compassion conditional.

cast.name: Nadia Orlov
cast.portrait: A woman in her early thirties, straight dark hair cut short, light olive skin, grey eyes, plain faded slate flight suit; guarded, attentive expression.
cast.bio: Nadia grew used to making a small allocation last and dislikes being praised for needing so little. She wants her flight to remain useful without becoming an excuse for neglect. The distinction becomes difficult when refusing an impossible assignment means leaving a real request unanswered.

cast.name: Pavel Kresin
cast.portrait: A man in his early thirties, dark-blond hair, light skin, blue-grey eyes, plain charcoal flight suit with worn cuffs; alert, candid expression.
cast.bio: Pavel's first answer to a shortage is to offer more of himself. His courage is real, and so is his impatience with people who ask him to wait. He wants to be trusted with difficult work and has trouble recognizing when trust should include being told to rest.

cast.name: Vera Dolin
cast.portrait: A woman in her forties, brown hair in a practical bun with a few grey strands, pale skin, dark eyes, plain navy work jacket; unsentimental, strong expression.
cast.bio: Vera keeps the serviceability board where everyone can see it. She has spent years preventing a temporary workaround from becoming an invisible permanent requirement. She will help a pilot attempt something difficult; she will not help an office pretend the difficulty was never there.

cast.name: Milan Sarek
cast.portrait: A man in his late thirties, short black hair, medium-brown skin, dark eyes, plain dark service shirt with an unmarked headset; tired, watchful expression.
cast.bio: Milan sees transport requests arrive from people who have already been told to ask somewhere else. He knows that a stamp can represent accountability or another locked door. He tries to leave a trail clear enough for an honest person to follow, even when honesty is an inconvenient qualification.
